newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds may shed U.S. can business.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds may shed U.S. can business.

text.p: As part of its effort to streamline operations, Reynolds Metals Co is considering selling off all or part of its $1 billion U.S. aluminum can business, The Wall Street Journal said.

In Wednesday's electronic edition, the paper said that as part of the effort, Reynolds is reducing its staff in Richmond, Va., which could result in the loss of 25 percent to 50 percent of the company's 1,800 corporate, research and development and engineering workers there.

The paper cited "people familiar with the company and the plans" who said Reynold's domestic can unit, which has the capacity to make 18 billion aluminum cans a year, could fetch from $750 million to $1.25 billion in an outright sale.
The can business is one of several units that Reynolds is considering selling, the article said.
Reynolds has partial interest in various can operations overseas, which also might be sold, the story said.
According to the paper, one person familiar with the company's plans said a transaction with the can unit was "imminent."
The newspaper quoted a Reynolds spokesperson who said the company would not comment on the "speculation."
